newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand sees big drop in 1996/97 coffee exports.
newsitem.headline: Thailand sees big drop in 1996/97 coffee exports.

text.p: Thailand said its 1996/97 (October-November) coffee exports are expected to plummet to 32,000 tonnes from 60,000 tonnes in the previous year due to a sharp drop in output and increased local demand.

Deputy commerce minister Chalermphol Chalermwongchai told reporters after a coffee policy meeting that the government would buy coffee for export from farmers at a guaranteed price of 30 baht a kg ($1.20).
The output for this crop year is expected to drop to 62,000 tonnes from around 81,398 tonnes forecast earlier because of rains, he said.
Higher local demand, which was seen at 30,000 tonnes, also cut down the amount available for exports, Chalermphol said.
Thailand produced 78,801 tonnes of coffee beans in 1995/96 but managed to ship 60,000 tonnes abroad.
The commerce ministry would sell the coffee beans it bought from farmers to exporters, possibly through tender, he said.

Commerce Minister Narongchai Akrasanee said recently that the outlook for Thai coffee exports was bleak as world prices were not bullish and the production cost of Thai coffee was much higher than that from Vietnam.
